question: On the Airbus A320, how are the wing fuel tanks divided?

options.a: Into forward and aft cells
options.b: Into inner and outer cells
options.c: Into three separate compartments: inner, mid, and outer

justification: As described in the system overview, the wing tanks on the A318, A319, and A320 are divided into inner cells and outer cells to manage structural loads.

question: Where is the center fuel tank physically located in the aircraft structure?

options.a: In the aft fuselage tail cone
options.b: In the center fuselage area as part of the center wing box
options.c: In the belly fairing underneath the cargo compartment

justification: The training manual states that the center tank is a part of the center wing box located in the center fuselage area.

question: What is the normal sequence of fuel supply to the engines when all tanks are full?

options.a: The wing inner cells are used first, followed by the center tank
options.b: The center tank is used first, then the wing inner cells
options.c: Fuel is drawn simultaneously from the center tank and wing outer cells

justification: Per the system overview, fuel is supplied to the engines from the center tank first. When the center tank is empty, fuel is then supplied from the wing inner cells.

question: Why is the fuel in the wing outer cells not used until the fuel load in the inner cells decreases to a low level?

options.a: To prevent fuel freezing in the outboard sections of the wing
options.b: To ensure less structural load on the wings
options.c: To provide a backup supply specifically for the APU

justification: The document specifies that to have less structural load on the wings, fuel in the outer cells is not used until the inner cell quantity decreases to a low level.

question: How is fuel transferred from the outer cells to the inner cells in the A320 wing tanks?

options.a: By two electrically driven scavenge pumps
options.b: By two inter cell transfer valves via gravity
options.c: By motive flow from the center tank jet pumps

justification: The description of the fuel system confirms that two inter cell transfer valves are used to transfer fuel from the outer cells to the inner cells by gravity when quantity reaches a low level.

question: Which actions cause the engine Low Pressure (LP) fuel valve to close?

options.a: The related engine reaches 95% N1 or the fuel pump fails
options.b: The related engine stops or the related FIRE pushbutton is released
options.c: The crossfeed valve is opened or the center tank becomes empty

justification: The manual states the LP valve is installed to stop fuel supply and closes when its related engine stops or when the FIRE pushbutton is released.

question: How many DC motors operate the fuel crossfeed valve?

options.a: One AC motor for normal operation and one DC motor for emergency
options.b: Two DC motors
options.c: A single dual-coil DC motor

justification: The technical description of the crossfeed valve specifies that it is electrically controlled and operated by two DC motors.

question: In the Airbus A321 fuel system, how is fuel moved from the center tank to the wing tanks?

options.a: Using two electric booster pumps in the center tank
options.b: Using transfer valves and two jet pumps
options.c: By gravity through intercell transfer valves

justification: On the A321, transfer valves control fuel transfer from the center tank to the wing tanks using pressure for two jet pumps installed in the center tank.

question: According to the general maintenance notes, what is the minimum fuel tank capacity required for the water drain valves to operate satisfactorily?

options.a: Minimum 5% of capacity
options.b: Minimum 10% of capacity
options.c: Minimum 1500 kg per wing

justification: A specific note in the water drain valve operation section states to make sure fuel tanks are filled to a minimum of 10% capacity to cover the valve outlet.

question: What occurs when the manual plunger on a refuel valve is pushed during refueling?

options.a: It resets the high-level sensor
options.b: It holds the valve open in case of an electrical failure
options.c: It bypasses the refuel coupling and allows gravity filling

justification: The document states that each refuel valve has a manual plunger which, when pushed, holds the valve open if an electrical failure occurs during refueling.

question: Which component electrically controls the landing gear and door sequencing?

options.a: The Braking Steering Control Unit (BSCU)
options.b: The Landing Gear Control and Interface Units (LGCIU)
options.c: The Flight Management and Guidance Computers (FMGC)

justification: The system overview for ATA 32 states that LGCIU 1 and 2 electrically control the gear and door sequencing.

question: When does the active LGCIU change over to the standby unit during normal operation?

options.a: Every 5 minutes automatically
options.b: After each retract/extend cycle when the L/G control lever is moved away from the DOWN position
options.c: Only upon a detected hardware failure in the active unit

justification: The manual states that the active unit changes after each retract/extend cycle when the L/G control lever is moved away from the DOWN position.

question: What is the effect of rotating the gravity extension crank handle for the first 1.5 turns?

options.a: It releases the landing gear downlocks
options.b: It operates the cut-out valve and vent valves to depressurize the system
options.c: It mechanically unlocks the nose gear doors only

justification: The description of Free Fall extension states that rotating the handle initially (up to 1.5 turns) operates the cut-out valve and vent valves to depressurize the system by connecting it to return.

question: The MLG shock absorber is a two-stage unit. Which of the following describes its configuration?

options.a: One oil chamber and one nitrogen chamber
options.b: Four chambers: first stage gas, recoil, compression, and second stage gas
options.c: Two identical chambers separated by a floating piston

justification: The MLG shock absorber description identifies four chambers: a first stage gas chamber, a recoil chamber, a compression chamber, and a second stage gas chamber.

subtopic: Main Landing Gear - Spare Seal Valve
question: What is the purpose of the spare-seal activating-valve on the MLG main fitting?

options.a: To drain hydraulic fluid during servicing
options.b: To isolate the bottom gland seals and activate the top gland seals if a leak occurs
options.c: To manually release the gear uplock during maintenance

justification: The manual states the spare-seal activating-valve can isolate the bottom gland seals if a leak occurs, transferring the pressure differential to the upper seal.

question: Normal braking is available when the Green hydraulic system pressure is available and which other condition is met?

options.a: The Yellow hydraulic system is at maximum pressure
options.b: The Parking Brake control switch is in the OFF position
options.c: The aircraft is moving at a speed greater than 70 knots

justification: Normal braking requires Green pressure, Anti-Skid switch ON, and the Parking Brake control switch in the OFF position.

question: At what threshold does the Alternate Braking Control Unit (ABCU) activate alternate braking if normal pressure fails?

options.a: When pressure downstream of the normal selector valve drops below 70 bar
options.b: When pressure downstream of the normal selector valve drops below 90 bar (1320 PSI)
options.c: When Green system total pressure drops below 1500 PSI

justification: The document explicitly mentions that a pressure lower than 90 bar (1320 PSI) or all other normal braking failure lets the ABCU activate the ALTN braking mode.

question: During aircraft towing, what is the maximum permitted extension (dimension H) for the nose gear shock absorber to avoid cam damage?

options.a: 200 mm
options.b: 300 mm (11.8 inches)
options.c: 400 mm

justification: The maintenance tips for nose wheel steering state: 'Do not tow the A/C if the dimension H is more than 300 mm... you can cause damage to the internal centering cams'.

question: How many primary jacking points are used to lift the aircraft?

options.a: Two: one on the nose and one on the main gear
options.b: Three: one forward (A) and two outboard of the engines (B)
options.c: Four: two on the wings and two on the fuselage

justification: The Jacking section states there are 'Three jacking points... the forward point A is located forward of the nose landing gear. The points B are located outboard of the engine pylons'.

question: In the Braking/Steering Control Unit (BSCU), which system takes priority if both are powered up simultaneously?

options.a: System 1
options.b: System 2
options.c: The system that was active during the previous flight cycle

justification: The BSCU architecture states: 'If both systems are powered up at the same time, system 1 has priority.'

question: The Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) is a constant speed gas turbine engine. Where is it located?

options.a: In the forward cargo compartment
options.b: In the unpressurized tail cone
options.c: In the center wing box

justification: The APU system overview states that it is located in the unpressurized tail cone.

question: When does the APU air intake flap open?

options.a: When the APU reaches 7% RPM
options.b: When the APU MASTER Switch is set to ON
options.c: When the START pushbutton is pressed

justification: The description of the air intake flap states that it opens when the APU MASTER Switch is set to ON.

question: At approximately what APU speed does the Electronic Control Box (ECB) stop the electrical supply to the starter?

options.a: 50% (Honeywell) or 55% (APIC)
options.b: 75% for both variants
options.c: 95% when the AVAIL light comes on

justification: The manual sections for Honeywell 131-9A and APIC APS3200 state that the ECB stops the starter supply at around 50% speed for Honeywell and 55% for APIC.

question: Which of the following parameters will trigger an immediate APU protective shutdown by the ECB?

options.a: Inlet guide vane position mismatch of 2 degrees
options.b: High Oil Temperature (HOT) or Low Oil Pressure (LOP)
options.c: APU fuel pump pressure below 21.8 psi

justification: The protective shutdown parameters listed include High Oil Temperature (HOT) and Low Oil Pressure (LOP). Fuel pump pressure below 21.8 psi merely triggers the pump to run, not a shutdown.

question: What is the purpose of the APU de-oiling solenoid valve during a cold start?

options.a: To bypass the oil cooler
options.b: To reduce the oil pressure pump load by allowing air into the pump inlet
options.c: To prevent oil from entering the load compressor

justification: The de-oiling solenoid description states it reduces the oil pressure pump load during APU start by allowing air to enter the inlet of the oil supply pump.

question: When is the APU drain tank contents emptied through the drain mast?

options.a: Automatically when the tank is full
options.b: When the aircraft speed is above 200 kt
options.c: During every APU shutdown sequence

justification: The manual states the contents of the drain tank are removed through the drain mast when the A/C is above 200 kt due to the suction effect.

question: What is the recommended replacement interval for the APU Fuel Control Unit (FCU) fuel filter?

options.a: Every 1000 flight hours
options.b: Every 8500 flight hours
options.c: Only when the Differential Pressure Indicator (DPI) shows a clog

justification: The technical description of the FCU on page 485 states: 'Fuel filter replacement is recommended every 8500 Flight Hours.'

question: What is the consequence if the ECB detects a failure of both APU speed sensors?

options.a: The APU continues to run using the EGT backup logic
options.b: The ECB starts an automatic shutdown sequence
options.c: The APU switches to a fixed fuel schedule of 95% speed

justification: The Power Monitoring section states: 'The ECB starts the automatic shutdown sequence if there is a failure of the two speed sensors.'

question: Which component serves as the oil reservoir for the APU lubrication system?

options.a: A separate tank in the APU compartment
options.b: The accessory gearbox (AGB)
options.c: The load compressor scroll

justification: The APU basic description for the accessory gearbox states: 'The gearbox is also the oil reservoir for the APU lubrication system.'

question: What is the purpose of the 120-second cool-down cycle during an APU normal shutdown?

options.a: To allow the oil to drain back into the sump by gravity
options.b: To run the APU at a low stabilized temperature before stop
options.c: To ensure the AC generator is completely unloaded

justification: The cool-down state section explains that this function runs the APU at a low stabilized temperature before normal shutdown to prevent internal damage.

question: How many identical channels does the Fuel Quantity Indication Computer (FQIC) possess?

options.a: One main and one backup
options.b: Two identical channels
options.c: Three channels for voting logic

justification: The FQIC description states it has 'two identical channels' and 'the healthiest channel is in control'.

question: What is the function of the cadensicons in the fuel quantity indicating system?

options.a: To measure the fuel level at the rib boundaries
options.b: To measure the density and dielectric constant of the fuel
options.c: To provide high-level automatic shut-off signals

justification: The manual states 'The cadensicons give a signal to the computer in proportion to the density and the dielectric constant of the fuel... the fuel mass is calculated from this density value'.

question: In normal operation, what is the accuracy of the fuel mass calculation provided by the FQIC?
justification: Under normal operation, the FQIC calculates mass with an accuracy of 1%. In back-up operation (if density is lost), it drops to less than 3% to 4%.

question: Under what condition will the ECAM display the Fuel on Board (FOB) with two amber dashes?

options.a: When a single capacitance probe fails
options.b: When accuracy is degraded beyond 5%
options.c: When accuracy is degraded between 3% and 5% but not exceeding it
options.d: As long as accuracy is NOT degraded beyond 5%

justification: The document specifies: 'The ECAM displays the Fuel on Board (FOB) with two amber dashes as a degraded display, as long as the accuracy is not degraded beyond 5%'. This typically occurs in backup operation.

subtopic: Fuel Level Sensing - Low Level Sensors
question: At what fuel quantity trigger does the wing tank low level warning appear on ECAM?

options.a: 500 kg
options.b: 750 kg

justification: The manual states '3 low level sensors at a fuel level of 750 Kg (1653 lbs) in each wing tank are used for... generating the wing tank low level warning on ECAM when exposed to air for more than 30s.'

question: What is the maximum steering angle of the nose wheels when controlled by the steering hand wheels?

options.a: 6 degrees
options.b: 74 degrees
options.c: 95 degrees

justification: The BSCU transforms orders into N/WS angles. For hand wheels, the maximum is 74 degrees. For rudder pedals, it is 6 degrees. 95 degrees is the maximum towing angle.

question: How does the Brake Temperature Monitoring Unit (BTMU) transmit temperature data to the BSCU?

options.a: By a digital ARINC 429 bus
options.b: By a voltage between 1V and 9V representing 0 to 1000°C
options.c: By varying the frequency of an AC current between 50 and 100kHz

justification: The manual states: 'the BTMU delivers a voltage which varies between 1V and 9V corresponding to a temperature range of 0 to 1000°C'. The BSCU then digitizes this.

question: In the braking system, what is the procedure to reset a hydraulic fuse after troubleshooting a leak?

options.a: Cycle the Anti-Skid switch
options.b: Open its bleed screw
options.c: Apply 7 full pedal applications with the yellow system pressurized

justification: Under Maintenance Tips, the document states: 'After trouble-shooting, the hydraulic fuse needs to be reset by opening its bleed screw.'

question: While center tank pumps are supplying the engines, at what condition will the center tank pumps stop to allow the wing pumps to run?

options.a: When center tank quantity drops below 500 kg
options.b: When the wing tank inner cell reaches the FULL level sensor due to fuel recirculation
options.c: When the outer cell temperature reaches 52.5°C

justification: The pump logic section states: 'While fuel is supplied from the center tank, the wing tanks will stay full... if this occurs, the center tank pump stops when the inner cell gets to the FULL level sensor.'

question: In the ACT system, how is fuel normally transferred from the ACT to the center tank?

options.a: By an electric transfer pump in all flight phases
options.b: By cabin air pressurization
options.c: By motive flow from the engine feed line

justification: The ACT system presentation states: 'Fuel is automatically transferred from the ACT to the center tank... Cabin air pressure pressurizes the ACT for the FWD transfer.'

question: During automatic ACT fuel transfer, what is the specific condition required regarding the center tank high level sensor?

options.a: The sensor must be wet for at least five minutes
options.b: The sensor must have been dry for at least ten minutes
options.c: The sensor must be dry for at least two minutes

justification: According to the ACT System D/O, automatic FWD transfer occurs when, among other conditions, the center tank high level sensor has been dry for at least ten minutes.

question: What is the result of pushing the ACT P/BSW to the MAN position on the overhead panel?

options.a: It closes the center tank transfer valves and stops all transfer
options.b: It opens the fuel inlet valve, the fuel transfer valve, and energizes the ACT transfer pump
options.c: It initiates a high-level BITE test of the ACT sensors

justification: The manual states that for manual transfer, pushing the ACT P/BSW opens the fuel inlet valve, the fuel transfer valve, and energizes the ACT transfer pump.

question: Under what condition will the FAULT legend on the ACT P/BSW illuminate during automatic transfer?

options.a: When the ACT fuel quantity reaches the low level sensor
options.b: When the center tank has less than 3000 kg and one ACT still has more than 250 kg of fuel
options.c: When the cabin air pressure used for transfer exceeds 5 psi

justification: The text specifies that the FAULT legend comes on if the center tank has less than 3000 kg and one ACT has more than 250 kg during automatic FWD transfer.

question: What is the primary purpose of the vent protector located inside the NACA type intake duct?

options.a: To prevent the entry of fuel into the surge tank
options.b: To prevent clogging of the vent duct by ice formation
options.c: To reduce the risk of a ground fire igniting the fuel tanks

justification: The Venting System Description states: 'The function of the vent protector is to prevent clogging of the vent duct by ice formation.'

question: Into which tank does the center tank vent system terminate?

options.a: The RH vent surge tank
options.b: The LH vent surge tank
options.c: The wing outer cells directly

justification: The manual states: 'The center tank vents into the LH vent surge tank.'

question: How is fuel that spills into the vent surge tank during normal operation returned to the main tanks?

options.a: By gravity through the rubber check valves
options.b: By a scavenge jet pump using motive power from the wing fuel pumps
options.c: By the main fuel pumps during the next refuel cycle

justification: The manual describes that fuel spilled into the surge tank is induced back into the outer cell by a scavenge jet pump using motive power from the wing fuel pumps.

question: What is the function of the vent float valves fitted in the vent lines?

options.a: To allow fuel to drain from the vent gallery to the wing inner cell
options.b: To prevent fuel from passing into the vent lines during aircraft bank maneuvers
options.c: To provide a signal to the FQIC when the surge tank is full

justification: Vent float valves are positioned to permit air to vent but prevent fuel from passing in the vent lines during A/C bank maneuvers.

question: In the event of an excess pressure in the wing outer cell, where is the pressure relieved?

options.a: Overboard via the NACA intake
options.b: Into the wing inner cell via an overpressure protector on rib 15
options.c: Into the center tank via the relief valve

justification: The manual states: 'An excess pressure in the outer cell relieves fuel into the inner cell via an overpressure protector mounted on rib 15.'

question: What is the purpose of the vapor seal fabric membrane located below the center tank?

options.a: To prevent fuel leaks from entering the baggage compartment
options.b: To isolate the center tank from the air conditioning compartment below
options.c: To provide thermal insulation for the APU fuel supply line

justification: The manual defines the vapor seal as a fabric membrane that isolates the center tank from the air conditioning compartment below.

question: If fuel is observed flowing from the drain mast, what component should be checked to determine the area of leakage?

options.a: The NACA intake flame arrestor
options.b: The leak monitor
options.c: The purge valve on the APU fuel line

justification: The manual states: 'In the event of fuel flowing from the drain mast, check the leak monitor to determine the area of leakage: center tank or APU fuel supply line.'

question: During normal extension, what is the prerequisite signal required by the LGCIU before it commands the landing gear to lower?

options.a: Landing gear control lever at DOWN for 5 seconds
options.b: All landing gear doors signaled as fully open
options.c: Green system pressure above 3000 PSI

justification: According to the normal extension sequence, 'When all doors are fully open, the LGCIU commands a gear extension'.

question: Which action does the LGCIU perform immediately after all landing gear are down and locked during an extension cycle?

options.a: It closes the safety valve to depressurize the system
options.b: It signals the doors to close while maintaining the gear extended signal
options.c: It sends a reset signal to the BSCU to allow braking

justification: The sequence states: 'When all the gear are down and locked, the LGCIU signals the doors to close... while maintaining the gear extended signal.'

question: What happens if the LGCIU detects that one of the shock absorbers is still compressed when the L/G control lever is moved to UP?

options.a: The gear retracts but the doors remain open
options.b: The lever is locked in the DOWN position by the baulk solenoid
options.c: The system automatically switches to LGCIU 2

justification: The 'L/G Baulk Solenoid' section explains it prevents gear retraction if any shock absorber is compressed to ensure the aircraft is not on the ground.

question: Which component of the MLG assembly is designed to decrease landing vibrations through the torque links?

options.a: The lock stay actuator
options.b: The torque link damper
options.c: The secondary shock absorber stage

justification: The manual states: 'The torque link damper... its function is to decrease the landing vibrations through the torque links.'

question: How is the correct replenishment level of the torque link damper verified when it is pressurized?

options.a: By checking the ECAM WHEEL page
options.b: By observing the FULL and REFILL level indications on the reservoir can extension
options.c: By measuring the H dimension on the MLG main fitting

justification: The manual states: 'When the contents are correct, the FULL and REFILL level indications are in view' based on the extension of the reservoir can.

question: At what angle is the nose gear sliding tube inclined forward to decrease the shimmy effect?

options.a: 6 degrees
options.b: 9 degrees
options.c: 15 degrees

justification: The NLG Sliding Tube description on page 343 confirms: 'It is inclined 9 degrees forward... to decrease the shimmy effect.'

question: How are the nose wheels automatically returned to the center position when the shock absorber is fully extended in flight?

options.a: By the BSCU sending a 0 degree command to the servo valve
options.b: By the engagement of two centering cams inside the shock absorber
options.c: By hydraulic pressure from the Blue system

justification: The manual describes that 'the pressure of the nitrogen causes the cams to engage... the wheels then return automatically to the center position' when extended.

question: Before any selection of the ground door opening control handle can be made, what hydraulic condition must be met?

options.a: The system must be completely depressurized
options.b: A pressure greater than 70 bar must be supplied to port B to retract the locking plunger
options.c: Yellow system pressure must be at 3000 PSI to override the uplock

justification: The document specifies: 'Before any selection can be made, a hydraulic pressure greater than 70 bar (1015 psi) must be supplied to port B to retract the locking plunger.'

question: During ground door opening, what component prevents the door from causing a hydraulic lock as it moves by gravity?

options.a: The hydraulic fuse
options.b: The door by-pass valve
options.c: The shuttle valve

justification: The manual states the system includes a by-pass valve which prevents a hydraulic lock and allows fluid to be released as the door moves by gravity.

question: When jacking the aircraft for a landing gear swing test, when must the safety stay (safety jack) be removed?

options.a: Before the aircraft is lifted off the ground
options.b: After the aircraft is stable on the three main jacks
options.c: The safety stay must be removed specifically for the gear swing

justification: The manual states: 'The safety stay must be removed for the gear swing.'

question: On the modified (New) APU system, from where is the residual fuel purged during shutdown?

options.a: From the fuel manifold only
options.b: From the pilot fuel injectors and manifold
options.c: From the FCU scavenge line

justification: The modification comparison table (page 667) shows that for the New System, the residual fuel source is 'Pilot fuel injectors and manifold'.

question: In the New APU system, what happens when the oil pressure increases to a specific value according to the ECB procedure?

options.a: A maintenance message is sent without shutdown
options.b: An automatic shutdown is triggered before a maintenance message is sent
options.c: The de-oiling valve opens to relieve pressure

justification: The modification table shows the new ECB procedure for pressure to a specific value is 'Automatic shutdown and maintenance message'.

question: Where is the Low Oil Pressure (LOP) switch relocated to in the new APU configuration?

options.a: Right side of air inlet plenum
options.b: RH side of Accessory Gearbox (AGB)
options.c: Directly on the oil cooler inlet

justification: The modification table specifies the LOP relocation for the New System is to the 'RH side of AGB near 3 o'clock position'.

question: What is the new destination for air supplied from the air inlet plenum in the modified APU system?

options.a: Air supplied to gearbox fan
options.b: Air supplied to cooling fan
options.c: Air supplied to the turbine plenum directly

justification: The modification table identifies the air inlet plenum airflow for the New System as 'Air supplied to cooling fan'.

question: The ECB uses the resistor-type engine identification module to determine which piece of data?

options.a: The current EGT limit
options.b: The APU serial number
options.c: The total number of operating hours

justification: The manual states: 'The resistor-type module transmits the APU serial number to the Electronic Control Box.'

question: What type of BITE system computer is the APU ECB classified as for Centralized Maintenance System (CMS) interfacing?

options.a: Type 1
options.b: Type 2
options.c: Type 3

justification: Page 662 confirms: 'The ECB is a BITE system type-1 computer and connects to the Centralized Fault Display System (CFDS)'.

question: During APU cowl door opening, why must the three quick release fasteners on the left door be correctly stowed?

options.a: To allow the shoot bolts to engage
options.b: To prevent damage to the seal on the APU left access door
options.c: To ensure the telescopic strut can be attached

justification: The WARNING on page 669 states: 'Make sure that the three quick release fasteners on the APU left access door are correctly stowed. This prevents damage to the seal'.

question: How many turns of the manual drive are required to fully cycle the APU inlet actuator on the variant that requires the most movement?

options.a: 47 turns
options.b: 87 turns
options.c: 120 turns

justification: The MEL/Deactivation section for APU inlet failure identifies two actuator types: one requiring 47 turns and the other 87 turns.

question: According to environmental precautions, what should be done with unused ground service equipment (GPU/Air conditioning cart) when no work is being performed?

options.a: Leave them in standby mode for quick restart
options.b: Turn them off to avoid unnecessary use of resources and noise
options.c: Leave them running if the APU is not in use

justification: The environmental precautions section advises: 'Turn-off unused ground service equipment (GPU, Air conditioning cart, etc...) if no work is being done'.

question: What specific action must be taken before starting the APU after it has been installed, to prevent a hot start?

options.a: Perform a 5-minute dry crank
options.b: Bleed the APU fuel line
options.c: Perform a BITE test of the IGV actuator

justification: Under APU Removal / Installation (WARNING), the manual states: 'After APU installation, bleed the APU fuel line before you start the APU to prevent hot start.'

question: The Fuel Diverter and Return Valve (FDRV) returns hot fuel to which location?

options.a: The center tank
options.b: The wing outer cell
options.c: The wing inner cell directly

justification: The principle of the IDG cooling system states: 'A Fuel Diverter and Return Valve (FDRV) lets the hot fuel return to the outer cell.'

question: What is the maximum temperature the IDG return valve maintains for the fuel returned to the tank?
justification: The manual states the return valve mixes hot fuel with cold fuel 'to keep the temperature of the returned fuel less than 100°C (212°F)'.

question: The FDRV closes if the fuel temperature in the outer cell reaches what threshold to prevent wing tank overtemperature?
justification: The section 'Outer Cell High Temperature' states the FDRV closes if the fuel temperature is too high in the outer cell, i.e. 52.5°C.

question: At what low level threshold does the IDG cooling stop to prevent an increase in unusable fuel in the wing tank?

options.a: 200 kg
options.c: 500 kg

justification: The IDG shut-off sensor stops IDG cooling when the fuel quantity in the inner cell is less than 280 kg.

question: How many bolts and pins attach the brake assembly to the axle flange of the main landing gear?

options.a: Six bolts and twelve pins
options.b: Three bolts and nine pins
options.c: Two bolts and six pins

justification: The Brake Assembly description (page 376) states: 'Three bolts and nine pins attach the brake to the axle flange of the landing gear.'

question: In the event of an aborted take-off, when is maximum braking pressure sent to the normal brake pistons if MAX mode is armed?

options.a: 2 seconds after V1 is reached
options.b: As soon as ground spoilers deployment order is present
options.c: When the reverse thrust levers are pulled

justification: The manual states for MAX mode: 'in the event of an aborted take-off, maximum braking pressure is sent to the normal brake pistons as soon as ground spoilers deployment order is present.'

question: For landing, when is progressive pressure sent to the brakes in Medium (MED) mode?

options.a: Immediately upon touchdown
options.b: 2 seconds after the ground spoilers deployment order
options.c: 4 seconds after the ground spoilers deployment order

justification: The document specifies: 'MEDium or LOw modes are selected for landing: progressive pressure is sent to the brakes, for respectively 2 or 4 seconds after the ground spoilers deployment order.' (MED = 2s, LO = 4s).

question: The BSCU compares main gear wheel speeds with the aircraft speed provided by which source for anti-skid computation?

options.a: The Landing Gear Control and Interface Units (LGCIU)
options.b: The Air Data Inertial Reference Units (ADIRUs)
options.c: The engine FADEC computers

justification: The principle of Anti-Skid states that wheel speed is 'compared with the A/C speed supplied by the Air Data Inertial Reference Units (ADIRUs).'

question: At what ratio below the reference speed does the BSCU give brake release orders to a wheel to prevent skidding?

options.a: 0.50 times the reference speed
options.b: 0.87 times the reference speed
options.c: 0.95 times the reference speed

justification: The anti-skid principle states: 'When the speed of a wheel decreases below 0.87 times the reference speed, brake release orders are given to that wheel.'

question: What is the maximum number of full brake pedal applications available using the accumulator pressure only?

options.a: 3 applications
options.b: 7 applications
options.c: 10 applications

question: What type of electrical power is used to drive the APU fuel pump motor?

options.a: 28V DC
options.b: 115V AC, 400Hz, single phase
options.c: 115V AC, 400Hz, three phase

question: At what pressure threshold does the APU fuel pump automatically stop running when the inlet pressure is sufficient?

options.a: Above 15.8 psi

question: How is the APU fuel Low Pressure (LP) valve actuated?

options.a: By fuel muscle pressure

options.c: By a pneumatic butterfly actuator

question: Which component allows the APU fuel pump to operate and the LP fuel valve to open for purging without having the APU Master Switch ON?

options.a: The APU start contactor bypass
options.b: The switch labeled FUEL VENT PUSH on the forward firewall
options.c: The manual override button on the FCU

justification: Under Maintenance Tips (page 684), it is explained that the switch labeled 'FUEL VENT PUSH' allows the APU pump to operate and the LP valve to open without the APU Master Switch ON for purging air after maintenance.

question: Under what condition will the 'FUEL LOW PRESSURE' message be displayed on the APU ECAM page?

options.a: APU speed is above 7% and fuel pressure is lower than 15.8 psi

options.c: Immediately upon releasing the APU Master Switch to OFF

question: When performing a light test (LTS) on the refuel/defuel control panel 800VU, what indication should be visible on the fuel quantity displays?

options.a: All zeros
options.b: All eights
options.c: The last recorded fuel mass

justification: The test switch section states: 'A filament test is done when the TEST switch is set to Lights. All the panel lights come on and all quantity indications show 8s.'

question: What is indicated by a blue light on the refuel/defuel control panel?

options.a: The refuel valve is in the manual position
options.b: The associated high level sensor is covered
options.c: Automatic refueling has completed

justification: The 'High Level Lights' section states: 'A blue High Level light for each tank comes on when the associated high level sensor is covered.'

question: What is the critical safety consideration when operating a refuel valve using the manual plunger?

options.a: The valve will not close unless the tank is full
options.b: There is no High Level protection
options.c: Fuel cannot be transferred to the center tank

justification: The Manual Refuel Valve Operation section explicitly warns: 'The most important thing to remember is that there is NO High Level protection when operating the refuel valve with the manual plunger.'

question: Which unit provides Landing Gear compressed information (ground/flight signal) to the FQIC?

options.a: LGCIU 1
options.b: LGCIU 2

question: In the event that cadensicon signals are invalid or lost, which signal is used by the FQIC as a backup for calculations?

options.a: The manual MLI values
options.b: The Capacitance Index Compensator (CIC) signal
options.c: The ADIRU longitudinal acceleration data

justification: Under Operational Principle, the manual states: 'If the cadensicon signal is not available or invalid... the Capacitance Index Capacitor (CIC) signal is used.'

question: During gear retraction, what action does the LGCIU perform immediately after the gear uplock proximity detectors signal that the gear is uplocked?

options.a: It closes the gear selector valve
options.b: It signals the doors to close while maintaining the gear raise signal
options.c: It depressurizes the nose wheel steering hydraulic block

justification: The retraction sequence (page 313) says: 'When all the L/G is up and locked... the LGCIU signals the doors to close while maintaining L/G UP signal to keep the raise line pressurized.'

question: The LGCIUs send up to six signals to the L/G indicator panel. These signals are primarily based on analyzing which inputs?

options.a: Shock absorber extension and hydraulic pressure
options.b: Gear uplock and downlock signals
options.c: Brake temperature and tire pressure

justification: The 'ARINC and Indicator Panel' section states: 'After analyzing gear uplock and down lock signals, the LGCIU sends up to six signals to the corresponding lights on the L/G indicator panel.'

question: How is normal landing gear operation restored after a free fall extension has been performed?

options.a: By resetting the LGCIU circuit breakers
options.b: By rotating the crank handle 3 turns counter-clockwise
options.c: By recycling the landing gear lever to UP then DOWN

justification: The Free Fall Extension section contains a specific note: 'Normal L/G operation is restored by rotating the crank handle 3 turns counter-clockwise.'

subtopic: Main Landing Gear - Shock Absorber Servicing
question: When checking the nitrogen charge of the MLG shock absorber, what dimension must be measured and recorded?

options.a: Dimension L

question: What is the maximum towing angle permitted on each side of the aircraft centerline?

question: What visual indication is used to check the overall wear of the brake heat pack?

question: How is the tire pressure signal transmitted from the wheel to the stationary axle in the TPIS?

options.b: By means of a rotating transformer

question: On the Honeywell APU, where does the load compressor cavity drain directly to?

options.a: The drain tank

options.c: Back to the gearbox sump

justification: The Honeywell drain system description states: 'The oil is drained directly overboard through the drain mast' for the load compressor cavity.

question: During a normal start on the Honeywell variant, between what APU speed range is the ignition switched to ON?

options.a: Between 0% and 55%

question: What component is used to move the Inlet Guide Vanes (IGVs) on the Honeywell 131-9A load compressor?

options.a: An electric stepper motor

options.c: A pneumatic piston using bleed air

question: Where is the Honeywell 131-9A compressor discharge pressure sensor (PT) located?

options.a: On the turbine exhaust cone
options.b: On the front of the air inlet plenum
options.c: Inside the accessory gearbox housing

question: How does the Honeywell 131-9A Electronic Control Box (ECB) protect the load compressor from surge conditions?

options.a: By immediately shutting down the APU
options.b: By modulating the surge control valve to discharge excess air into the exhaust
options.c: By increasing the fuel flow to the power section to increase RPM

question: What determines the opening angle of the Inlet Guide Vanes (IGVs) during APU operation?

options.a: The amount of electrical load on the generator only

options.c: The altitude signal from the ADIRUs

justification: The IGV opening angle depends on the bleed air demand for the Main Engine Start (MES) system and the Environmental Control System (ECS).

question: During APU running at 99%, what is the response of the Surge Control Valve (SCV) when the APU Bleed pushbutton is selected ON?

options.a: The SCV moves to the fully open position
options.b: The SCV moves to the closed position and then modulates to prevent surge
options.c: The SCV remains in the standby position until engine start is initiated

justification: To make sure a pressure build-up occurs in the Aircraft Bleed supply duct, the ECB commands the SCV to the closed position and then to modulate.

question: What is the consequence of a failure in the load compressor control system on a Honeywell 131-9A APU?

options.a: The IGVs are forced fully open and the SCV is closed
options.b: The IGVs are closed and the bleed control valve is fully opened to discharge
options.c: The APU fuel flow is limited to 50% to prevent overspeed

justification: A specific note in the manual states: 'In case of failure of the load compressor control, the IGVs are closed and the bleed control valve is fully opened to discharge.'

question: How is the pneumatic load managed by the ECB if an APU over-temperature condition is detected during steady-state operation?

options.a: The pneumatic load is increased to use more cooling air

options.c: The APU is immediately shut down without any modulation

justification: EGT control logic reduces pneumatic load first to give priority to electrical load by controlling the position of the IGVs to the closed position.

question: What feedback sensor does the Honeywell 131-9A Surge Control Valve use to transmit its position to the ECB?

options.a: A rotary potentiometer
options.b: A Linear Variable Differential Transducer (LVDT)
options.c: A micro-switch for open/closed only

justification: The document states: 'The SCV (with an LVDT) send valve position feedback back to the ECB.'

question: In the event that the APU air intake flap fails to open, which of the following is correct?

options.a: The APU will start but EGT will be higher
options.b: The air intake flap can be opened manually by a manual override device
options.c: The ECB will bypass the flap signal if ground speed is zero

justification: The manual states: 'In case of failure, the air intake flap can be opened or closed manually by a manual override device.'

question: What is the action of the ECB if reverse flow operation is detected in the APU air system?

options.a: It closes the bleed control valve only
options.b: The APU is automatically shut down by the ECB
options.c: It opens the surge control valve to maximum

justification: A specific note (page 635) states: 'In case of detected reverse flow operation, the APU is automatically shut down by the ECB.'

question: How many Inlet Guide Vanes (IGVs) are installed on the APIC APS3200 load compressor?

options.a: 16 IGVs

options.c: 32 IGVs

question: What component on the APIC APS3200 acts as a combined bleed and surge valve?

options.a: The Load Control Valve
options.b: The Bleed Control Valve
options.c: The Bypass SCV

justification: The manual states for APIC: 'The bleed control valve acts as a combined bleed and surge valve, electrically controlled by the ECB and fuel operated.'

question: On the APIC APS3200, what is used as the hydraulic fluid for the servo valve actuator to control the IGVs?

options.a: Aircraft Green system hydraulic fluid
options.b: APU fuel
options.c: APU engine oil

justification: The APIC IGV section specifies: 'The IGV system uses fuel as hydraulic fluid for the servo valve actuator to control the IGVs through the ECB.'

question: Where is the bleed air from the APIC APS3200 load compressor diverted when it is not selected for the aircraft pneumatic system?

options.a: Directly overboard via the drain mast
options.b: To the APU exhaust
options.c: Back to the compressor inlet plenum

justification: For the APIC variant: 'The fuel-operated bleed control valve is a diverter valve: either to the A/C system and/or the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) exhaust.'

question: What provides direct current to the APIC ECB for up to 230ms if the main aircraft power supply is interrupted?

options.a: The A/C Hot Battery Bus
options.b: The Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG) in the cooling fan
options.c: A dedicated capacitor module in the ECB

justification: The oil cooling section for APIC states: 'The cooling fan incorporates a Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG), which supplies a direct current to the Electronic Control Box (ECB)... for a maximum of 230ms.'

question: During engine start with an APIC APU, what is the initial position commanded for the IGVs?

options.a: 22 degrees open

question: What is the result of pushing the Pack P/B while the APIC APU is running at 99% with Bleed ON?

options.b: The ECB sends an extend command to move the IGVs into a more open position

question: What does the APIC ECB use to calculate the compressor air flow for ECAM indication?

options.b: APU RPM and IGV position feedback

question: In the APIC APS3200, what happens to the bleed control valve when the APU is shut down?

justification: The manual states: 'When the APU is shut down, it vents the unused air to the APU exhaust.'

question: What is the status of the IGVs if a failure occurs in the APIC IGV control loop?

options.a: They are forced to the 22 degree position
options.b: The IGVs are closed
options.c: They default to the position required for max electrical load

justification: A specific note on page 635 states: 'In case of IGV control failure, the IGVs are closed.'

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six sequences controlled by the APU management system?

options.a: Watch state
options.b: In-flight cruise state

question: During the APU power-up state, which component is tested for ROM checksum and RAM read/write?

options.a: The Data Memory Module
options.b: The On Board Replaceable Module (OBRM)
options.c: The ECAM Display Unit

justification: The power-up state description includes a 'test of On Board Replaceable Module (OBRM), Read Only Memory (ROM) checksum, Random Access Memory (RAM) read/write'.

question: What logic must the ECB satisfy to transition from the Watch state to the Start Preparation state?

options.a: Rotation speed must be greater than 7% RPM
options.b: Rotation speed must be less than or equal to 7% RPM
options.c: Fuel pressure must be above 23.2 psi

justification: The manual states: 'Upon receipt of the start command... and rotation speed is less than or equal to 7% rpm, the ECB enters the start preparation state.'

question: When does the APU transition from the Starting state to the Steady state (Run state)?

options.a: At 60% speed when the ignition is de-energized

question: At what threshold is the APU speed reduced to 99% for fuel saving reasons on the ground?

question: During a normal shutdown, which protection circuit does the ECB test by simulating a specific condition?

options.c: Fire detection loop A/B

question: What is the required APU speed during a shutdown sequence before the starter motor can be re-engaged?

options.a: Below 15% RPM

question: At what speed during the shutdown sequence does the gearbox de-oil solenoid valve open on the APIC APU?

options.a: Less than 95% rpm

question: What initiates an immediate APU shutdown without time delay, even if bleed air is in use?

options.c: Detection of aircraft electrical power transients

question: Which aircraft computer provides the 'aircraft on ground' discrete signal to the APU ECB?

options.b: LGCIU 1
options.c: FWC 1

question: Where does the ECB send indications to be displayed on the ECAM APU page?

options.c: Through the Flight Warning Computers (FWC)

question: How does the ECB know whether to follow Technical Standard Order (TSO) or Joint Aviation Requirements (JAR) for shutdown logic?

question: Which system provides the APU speed signal as a backup for overspeed protection to the ECB?

options.b: The Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG)

question: Which component manages the APU lifetime data, such as operating hours and starts?

options.c: The SDAC 1

question: Before APU removal, what action must be performed on the Centralized Fault Display System (CFDS)?

question: What precaution must be taken when opening the APU access door regarding the door mechanism?

options.c: The A/C must be grounded to the main gear only

question: According to Airbus recommendations, when should APU oil servicing be performed if a 'LOW OIL LEVEL' advisory appears?

question: What is the capacity of each vent surge tank on the Airbus A321?

options.b: The left wing tank

question: Which condition must be met for the center tank high level sensor before the ACTs can be defueled into the center tank?

options.b: The sensor must be dry to ensure there is enough space

question: Why are aluminum structural items in the wing and center boxes given a specific finishing during production?

options.b: Wiring is limited to low energy requirements and uses external electrical wiring support clamps

justification: Page 237 explains that wiring is limited to systems with very low energy requirements and uses external electrical wiring support clamps to ensure a cut cable cannot contact the fuel tank boundary.

question: What is the specific requirement for wire locking fasteners inside the fuel tanks according to safety procedures?

options.a: All wire locking must be installed or adjusted outside the fuel tank
options.b: Only stainless steel wire may be used inside the center tank
options.c: Wire locking must be coated with a specific fuel-resistant sealant

justification: Under 'Working Environment' on page 267, the manual specifies: 'all wire locking must be installed/adjusted outside the fuel tank.'

question: What color tie wraps are the only ones permitted for use inside the fuel tanks?

options.a: White
options.b: Blue
options.c: Red

justification: Page 267 explicitly states: 'Use only RED tie wraps in the fuel tanks.'

question: What is the maximum allowed fuel gas concentration (Lower Explosive Limit - LEL) before personnel can enter a fuel tank?

options.a: Less than 50% LEL
options.b: Less than 25% LEL
options.c: Less than 10% LEL

justification: Page 263 states: 'The fuel gas concentration must be < 10% of the Lower Explosive Limit (LEL) before entering into the tanks.'

question: Under what condition is it mandatory for maintenance personnel to use a respirator when working near open fuel tanks?

options.a: If any fuel remains in the tank
options.b: If the fuel-gas concentration is more than 5% of the LEL
options.c: Only when the temperature exceeds 30°C

justification: Page 263 provides the warning: 'You must use a respirator if the fuel-gas concentration in the fuel tanks is more than 5% of the Lower Explosive Limit (LEL).'

question: Which of the following is strictly prohibited for use inside fuel tanks during maintenance?

options.a: Lint-free cloths
options.b: Metallic wire wool
options.c: Protective rubber mats

justification: Page 267 carries the warning: 'Do not use metallic wire wool in fuel tanks.'

question: How many Magnetic Level Indicators (MLI) are installed in the center fuel tank?

options.a: One
options.b: Two
options.c: Four

justification: Page 277 states: 'There is one MLI in the center tank'.

question: For the Airbus A321 variant, how many MLIs are installed in each wing?

options.a: Three
options.b: Four
options.c: Five

justification: Page 277 and 278 specify that on the A321, there are 3 MLIs in each wing, compared to 4 on the A318/319/320.

question: When reading an extended MLI rod, which 'UNITS' mark is considered the correct reading?

options.a: The mark furthest from the wing skin
options.b: The mark nearest to the bottom skin of the wing
options.c: The average of the highest and lowest visible marks

justification: Page 277 states: 'read the UNITS mark nearest to the bottom skin of the wing.'

question: To determine the fuel volume in a wing tank with multiple MLIs, which indicator should be used primarily?

options.a: The most inboard MLI
options.b: The most outboard MLI that indicates fuel
options.c: The MLI located closest to the gravity refuel point

justification: Page 277 states: 'To determine the wing volume, use the most outboard MLI, which indicates fuel in the tank.'

question: What additional information is essential to convert MLI readings into an accurate fuel mass calculation?

options.a: Current fuel temperature only
options.b: Aircraft attitude (pitch and roll) and fuel specific density
options.c: The number of fuel pumps currently operating

justification: Pages 279 and 285 explain that aircraft attitude data and fuel specific density are essential for calculating the mass of fuel from MLI readings.

question: How can aircraft pitch and roll data be accessed in the cockpit for use with MLI fuel tables?

options.a: By reading the standby horizon only
options.b: Through the MCDU (AIDS menu or FQIS input parameters page)
options.c: By observing the position of the flight control surfaces on the ECAM F/CTL page

justification: Page 283 states that pitch and roll data can be selected through the MCDU via the AIDS menu or the CFDS FQIS INPUT PARAMETERS page.

question: If an MLI rod shows an odd number and the AMM tables only list even numbers, what action should the technician take?

options.a: Round up to the nearest even number
options.b: Interpolate between the nearest even numbers in the table
options.c: Use the next lower even number to be conservative

justification: Page 285 states: 'To calculate the volume of fuel for odd numbers, interpolate (divide the difference) between the nearest even numbers in the table.'

question: During a walk-around inspection, what does the absence of a white cross on a black background in the wing outer cell indicate?

options.a: The tank is completely full
options.b: A possible problem with the tank venting system (burst disc)
options.c: The high-level sensor is unserviceable

justification: Page 287 states: 'it is important to check the burst disc in the OUTER cell. A white cross should be visible... If it is not visible, it may indicate a problem with the tank venting system.'

question: When aircraft emergency electrical power is used, which pumps are supplied?

options.a: Both center tank pumps
options.b: Two wing fuel boost pumps, one in each wing
options.c: All four wing pumps simultaneously

justification: Page 287 states: 'When aircraft emergency electrical power is used, two wing fuel boost pumps will be supplied, one in each wing.'

question: During refueling operations, where should the bonding cable between the fuel tanker and the aircraft typically be connected?

options.a: To the wing tip static wicks
options.b: To the Nose or Main gear
options.c: To the engine exhaust cone

justification: Page 287 states: 'Connect a bonding cable between the fuel tanker and a grounding point on the aircraft, typically on the Nose or Main gear.'

question: Where are the charging valves for the MLG two-stage shock absorber located?

options.a: Both at the top of the main fitting
options.b: One at the top (Valve A) and one at the bottom (Valve B)
options.c: On the sliding tube near the axle

justification: The MLG shock absorber servicing section (page 445/446) identifies Valve A as the top charging valve and Valve B as the bottom charging valve.

question: What is the function of the nitrogen pressure in the MLG shock absorber second stage gas chamber?

options.a: To provide high-pressure damping for the initial touchdown
options.b: To provide high-pressure support for high-load taxiing and landing impacts
options.c: To act as a backup for the brake accumulator

justification: The shock absorber description identifies the second stage gas chamber as containing gas at a high pressure to handle the upper range of the landing and taxiing loads.

question: If a leak occurs at the MLG lower bearing housing, how is the spare seal activating valve used to troubleshoot?

options.a: The valve is opened to drain excess fluid into a container
options.b: The valve stem is screwed in to isolate the lower seal and transfer pressure to the upper seal
options.c: The valve is used to inject grease directly into the gland seal

justification: Page 441 explains that screwing on the valve stem 'isolates the lower seal from hydraulic pressure... and transfers the pressure differential to the upper seal.'

question: What must be confirmed about the A/C weight distribution before lifting the aircraft on jacks?

options.a: The fuel must be drained completely from the wing tanks
options.b: The weight of fuel must be applied equally on the two sides of the aircraft centerline

justification: Under 'Jacking Precautions' (page 421), the manual states: 'be sure that... the weight of fuel is applied equally on the two sides of the aircraft centerline.'

question: When servicing the torque link damper, what is the required hydraulic charging rig pressure range?

options.a: 1.5 to 2.0 bars
options.c: 5.0 to 7.5 bars

justification: The replenishment procedure for the torque link damper (page 443) specifies applying a pressure of 2.42 to 2.75 bars.

question: How much time is recommended to wait after taxiing or towing before checking shock absorber extension and pressures?

options.a: Minimum 2 minutes
options.b: Minimum 10 minutes
options.c: Exactly one hour

justification: Page 453 specifies: 'it is recommended that you wait a minimum of ten minutes after taxiing or towing before you carry out this procedure.'

question: Why is it necessary to center the nose wheels before resetting the steering function after towing?

options.a: To allow the BSCU to perform a BITE test
options.b: To avoid injury to personnel when the system is pressurized
options.c: To ensure the nose landing gear doors can close properly

justification: The maintenance tips for NWS (page 415) state: 'When resetting the steering function after towing, nose wheels must be centered to avoid injury.'

question: What is the requirement regarding tire pressure if a wheel assembly must be changed?

options.a: The tire must be pressurized to its nominal value
options.b: The tire must be fully deflated
options.c: The tire pressure should be reduced to 50% only

justification: Under 'Wheel removal' on page 436 and 439, it is specified to 'fully deflate the tire if it must be changed'.

question: What must be verified regarding the aircraft's orientation when performing an open-air jacking operation?

options.a: The aircraft must be pointing downwind
options.b: The aircraft must be pointing upwind
options.c: The aircraft must be perpendicular to the crosswind

justification: Under 'Jacking Limitations' (page 421), the manual states: 'In any condition, the aircraft must be pointing upwind.'

question: How is artificial feel provided at the brake pedals during manual braking?

options.a: By hydraulic pressure from the Blue system
options.b: By means of 2 sets of spring rods
options.c: By an electric torque motor controlled by the BSCU

justification: Page 382 states: 'The artificial feel at the pedals is provided by means of 2 sets of spring rods'.

question: During the APU power-up state, what happens to the ECAM display?

options.a: The APU page is automatically shown on the lower ECAM display unit

justification: Under 'POWER-UP STATE' (page 617), the manual states: 'on the lower ECAM display unit the APU page is shown.'

question: For the Honeywell 131-9A, what is the role of the P2 and T2 sensors during the start sequence?

options.a: They provide differential pressure for surge control
options.b: They provide air inlet pressure and temperature data to the ECB for fuel control
options.c: They monitor the EGT to prevent a hot start

justification: Under 'CONTROL' (page 483), it states: 'During start, it uses speed, EGT, air inlet pressure and temperature sensors (P2 and T2).'

question: What pressure does the Honeywell FCU actuator pressure regulator maintain for fuel muscle pressure?

options.a: 125 psig
options.b: 250 psig
options.c: 1500 psig

justification: The 'MUSCLE PRESSURE' section (page 487) states: 'Additionally fuel muscle pressure 250 psig operates the surge control valve actuator...'

question: Which of the following is considered an APU protective shutdown parameter?

options.a: Low fuel quantity in center tank
options.b: Clogged oil filter
options.c: Selection of APU Bleed to OFF

justification: The list of protective shutdown parameters (page 639) includes 'oil filter clogged'.

question: What causes an automatic APU emergency shutdown on the ground?

options.a: Oil temperature exceeding 135°C
options.b: Detection of an APU fire on ground
options.c: Loss of A/C electrical power

justification: Page 641 states: 'The ECB starts an automatic emergency shutdown when an APU FIRE is found on ground.'

question: How many water drain valves are located on the entire aircraft?

question: When performing the water contamination test using the purger tool, what indicates the presence of water?

options.a: The color stays yellow
options.b: The color goes from yellow to blue
options.c: The fuel becomes cloudy and white

justification: Page 19 states: 'When the colour stays yellow, there is no water in the test... The colour from the test goes from yellow to blue' if water is present.

question: According to the MPD, how often is it recommended to perform a regular draining of the fuel tank water content?

options.a: Every 24 hours
options.b: Every 36 hours (or less)
options.c: Only during A-Checks

justification: Page 273 states: 'The Maintenance Planning Document (MPD) recommends that operators perform this procedure every 36 hours (or less).'

question: How are the center tank fuel pumps replaced?

options.a: From the wing lower surface
options.b: Through access panels in the belly fairing
options.c: Through the forward cargo compartment floor

question: What is the purpose of the fuel pump canister?

options.a: To house the fuel filter and bypass valve

question: On the Refuel/Defuel control panel 800VU, what is the significance of a steady green END light?

options.a: The refuel gallery is pressurized

question: What is the function of the amber OPEN light on the refuel/defuel control panel?

options.c: It shows that a wing tank transfer valve is latched open

question: Under what circumstance will the green END light on the refuel panel flash?

options.a: When a high level sensor is triggered in any tank

question: What feature of the refuel/defuel coupling prevents damage to the aircraft structure if a sideways force is applied to the hose?

options.b: A breakaway groove around its circumference
options.c: A quick-release spring-loaded bypass mechanism

question: What is the purpose of the Multi Tank Indicator (MTI) on the refuel/defuel control panel?

question: What occurs on the external refuel control panel when the cockpit preselector PoWeR P/BSW is pushed?

options.c: The high level sensors are bypassed

question: What is the nominal refueling pressure required for automatic refuel operation?

options.a: 35 psi
options.b: 50 psi (3.45 bar)
options.c: 70 psi

justification: Under 'PREPARATION' for refuel operation (page 93), it notes: 'the nominal refueling pressure is 50 psi per square inch, i.e. 3.45 bar.'

question: On the Honeywell APU, at what speed does the ECB de-energize the start contactor if the aircraft is above 20,000 ft?

question: When the APU START pushbutton is pressed, what action does the ECB take after approximately 100 milliseconds?

options.c: It energizes the ignition exciter directly

question: If an APU flame-out occurs on the Honeywell variant after 60% speed, when will the ECB restart the ignition?

options.a: Only if speed drops below 50%

question: What component prevents the LGCIU from allowing the L/G control lever to be moved to the UP position if any shock absorber is compressed?

options.b: The baulk solenoid

question: Which aircraft computers send a signal to the landing gear safety valve to shut off hydraulic pressure when airspeed exceeds 260 kts?

options.a: LGCIU 1 and 2

question: At least how many ground spoiler extension signals from the Spoiler Elevator Computers (SECs) are required to activate the automatic braking system?

options.a: One

question: What does the illumination of the green DECEL light on the auto-brake panel indicate during landing?

question: Which of the following conditions will automatically disconnect the A/SKID regulation during alternate braking?

question: In the A321 fuel system, what provides the motive pressure for the two jet pumps used to transfer fuel from the center tank?

options.b: Transfer valves supplying pressure from the wing pumps

question: In AUTO mode on the ground with slats extended, why are the center tank pumps not running even if the pushbuttons are pressed?

options.c: To prevent air entering the pump canisters

question: How long do the center tank pumps automatically continue to run after the center tank reaches low level in cruise?

options.a: 2 minutes
options.b: 5 minutes
options.c: They stop immediately

question: What logic triggers the 'FUEL AUTO FEED FAULT' message on the EWD?

question: On the Honeywell 131-9(A) APU, what is the purpose of the turbine plenum drain orifice?

options.c: To vent excess pressure from the load compressor scroll

question: How is the vacuum created in the Honeywell APU drain line to remove the contents of the drain tank?

question: What type of interface connects the Honeywell APU drain lines to the right access door drain lines?

options.a: High-pressure threaded couplings

question: On the APIC APS 3200 APU, where does the oil leak from the front bearing seal flow?

question: How is the residual fuel in the APIC pilot injectors and manifold handled during shutdown?

options.b: It is purged to the APU exhaust

question: In the modified APIC APU drain system, which component is used instead of a direct 3 o'clock position drain mast for fluids?

question: How many 'door fully open' signals are provided for the nose landing gear doors to the LGCIUs?

question: For what purpose are wheel speed indications sent to the LGCIUs from the BSCU?

options.a: To control the door closure sequence after takeoff
options.b: For BITE inhibition
options.c: To calculate the landing distance for the FDIMU

justification: Under BSCU Control Interfaces (page 397), it is stated: 'LGCIUs receive wheel speed indications. These signals are used for BITE inhibition.'

question: During gear retraction, what causes the 'Nose Wheel Steering Disconnected' message to appear on the ECAM?

question: What is the requirement for the proximity sensors for nose landing gear 'ground' and 'wheels centered' signals?

question: How many capacitance probes are installed in each wing tank of the Airbus A320?

options.b: 14 probes

question: Which specific probes in the A320 fuel tanks contain diodes to measure fuel temperature?

options.a: Probes No. 1 and No. 5
options.b: Probe No. 2 (inner) and Probe No. 13 (outer)

question: Why is one probe equipped with a Capacitance Index Compensator (CIC) always fully submerged in fuel under normal conditions?

options.b: To determine the permittivity (dielectric constant) of the fuel
options.c: To prevent the pump from running dry

question: What components are used specifically on the Airbus A321 to measure fuel density instead of a standard cadensicon?

options.a: Densitometers and pressure transducers
options.b: Ultracomp and Dualcomp

question: How are fuel level signals processed by the FQIC to remove fluctuations before being displayed?

question: Which aircraft variant uses jack pad adapters that are NOT interchangeable with other A320 family members?

options.b: Airbus A319 Corporate Jet

question: When using the 'Quick Leveling Procedure' with the ADIRU, which codes are entered into the MCDU scratchpad to verify alignment?

question: If the ADIRUs are unavailable, where should the spirit level be placed for the alternate leveling method?

options.a: On the floor of the cockpit
options.b: On a track in the FWD cargo compartment
options.c: On the wing upper surface spar

question: What is the towing speed limitation dependent upon, according to the maintenance manual?

question: When installing a main wheel, what must be aligned on the brake rotor?

question: When are the intercell transfer valves automatically latched open?

options.c: When the aircraft reaches cruise altitude

question: Where is the fuel crossfeed valve located?

question: Where is the fuel air release valve installed in the system?

question: What is the function of the wing scavenge jet pump that connects to the vent surge tank?

options.b: The wing tank pumps (if running)
options.c: The engine-driven fuel pump

options.b: The constant Differential Pressure (DELTA P) valve

question: Where is the High Oil Temperature (HOT) sensor located on the Honeywell 131-9(A) APU?

options.a: The de-oiling solenoid valve remains open
options.b: The oil bypass valve opens to bypass the oil cooler

question: How is the generator scavenge oil processed before being supplied back to the oil reservoir on the Honeywell APU?

options.a: It passes through the air/oil separator only

question: What indication is available on the ground to identify impending oil filter clogging on the Honeywell APU?

options.a: A message on the ECAM STATUS page only

options.b: 33 psi
options.c: 35 psi

options.a: 33 psi
options.b: 35 psi

question: Which component manages the signal to close the Fuel Return Valve (FRV) if the wing tank temperature is too high?

options.a: The center tank pumps are restarted

options.c: The crossfeed valve is automatically opened

question: Which threshold triggers the FLSCU to command the FDRV closed due to an inner cell high temperature condition?
justification: Page 53 states: 'The FDRV closes if the fuel temperature in the inner cell is too high, i.e. 55°C (131°F).'

question: How does the FDRV respond to a 'Pump Pressure Loss' condition in the wings while in flight?

options.a: It opens fully to ensure cooling flow

question: If both wing tank pumps fail and the center tank is empty, what component allows the engine to be supplied with fuel?

options.a: The sequence valve
options.b: The bypass suction valve

question: What is the primary reason for closing the FDRV when the inner cell fuel quantity drops to 280 kg?

options.a: To prevent the IDG from overheating

question: Which aircraft computers provide ground spoiler extension signals to the BSCU for auto-brake activation?

question: Where is the Braking/Steering Control Unit (BSCU) physically located?

question: How does the BSCU communicate BITE data and failure messages to the Centralized Fault Display System (CFDS)?

options.b: By a bi-directional ARINC 429 link

question: What is the purpose of the 4 availability discretes sent from the BSCU to the FMGCs?

options.a: To calibrate the auto-brake deceleration rates
options.b: To meet the safety requirements of a category 3B landing
options.c: To synchronize the nose wheel steering with the autopilot

question: Which component part of the FDIMU collects maintenance data for preventive maintenance reports?

options.a: FDIU

options.c: SDAC 2

question: During a disagreement between the BSCU control and monitoring channels, what is the system response?

question: How many total proximity detectors are installed for the landing gear system that are listed as MMEL items?

options.b: To prevent gear retraction if any shock absorber is compressed

options.b: It is an external unit that exchanges data with the ECB

options.c: Single-phase induction motor

justification: The 'BRAKE FANS' description specifies: 'Each fan includes a three-phase type motor, an impeller and a shroud'.

question: If the brake fans are inoperative, how does this affect dispatch according to the BTMU section?

question: What visual indication identifies a possible problem with the tank venting system during a walk-around inspection?

options.c: The NACA intake being stuck in the closed position

question: What must be installed on the N/WS control lever before towing the aircraft?

options.a: The steering lockstay collar
options.b: The safety pin
options.c: A high-visibility warning flag only

justification: Page 415 states: 'Before towing, the N/WS control lever has to be in the deactivation position with the safety pin installed'.

question: When resetting the steering function after towing, what is the mandatory requirement for the nose wheels to avoid injury?

options.a: They must be turned to full 95 degrees

question: Which component of the brake assembly contains the hydraulically independent sets of pistons for normal and alternate braking?

options.a: The torque tube

question: What is the maximum number of pistons that may be found in a single brake unit piston set depending on the version?

options.a: 5 pistons

question: How are the normal and alternate braking systems isolated within a single brake assembly?

options.a: By an internal shuttle valve within the housing

question: What is the function of the self-sealing coupling on the brake assembly?

options.a: To allow for manual bleeding without tools

question: Which component provides the interface between the brake assembly and the aircraft wheel to transmit braking torque?

options.a: The wear indicator pins
options.b: The torque tube

question: What is the primary maintenance risk when applying grease to an axle sleeve near a very hot brake?

options.a: The grease will fail to lubricate correctly
options.b: The grease can burn and cause a fire
options.c: The grease will contaminate the carbon heat pack

justification: Page 436 provides a specific WARNING: 'You must not put too much grease on the axle sleeve. A very hot brake can cause the grease to burn and cause a fire.'

question: Which safety step is mandatory before attempting to remove a wheel for the purpose of a tire change?

options.a: Charge the brake accumulator
options.b: Fully deflate the tire
options.c: Apply the parking brake

justification: The 'Wheel removal' procedure (page 436/439) explicitly lists: 'fully deflate the tire if it must be changed'.

question: During wheel installation, what is the purpose of the 'pre-torque' value applied to the axle nut?

options.a: To permanently lock the bearings
options.b: To seat the components while turning the wheel
options.c: To calibrate the TPIS sensor

justification: The installation procedure states to 'adjust the torque meter to the pre-torque value and apply it to the nut while turning the wheel' to ensure correct seating before final torquing.

question: If a hydraulic leak is found on a brake assembly piston, what is the procedure for deactivation without removing the brake?

options.a: Cap the bleeder valve
options.b: Disconnect the self-sealing coupling
options.c: Insert a mechanical lockout pin in the housing

question: When installing the locking nuts for the wheel axle nut bolts, in which direction must the bolt heads face?

options.a: Facing away from the aircraft centerline
options.b: Facing the axle
options.c: Facing the outboard side of the wheel rim

question: What provides the pressure reading for the nitrogen pre-charge of the alternate braking system?

options.a: The triple pressure indicator in the cockpit

options.c: The ECAM WHEEL page

question: Which hydraulic system supplies the brake accumulator?

options.a: Green system
options.b: Yellow system
options.c: Blue system

justification: The system overview and page 409 state: 'The brake accumulator is supplied from the yellow hydraulic system'.

question: What must be done to the brake accumulator to check its nitrogen pre-charge as required by the MPD?

options.a: The system must be pressurized to 3000 PSI
options.b: The accumulator must be hydraulically depressurized using the relief valve
options.c: The aircraft must be placed on jacks

justification: Page 409 explains: 'The relief valve allows the hydraulic depressurization of the accumulator to check its nitrogen pre-charge'.

question: In the event of low yellow system pressure, what does the brake accumulator provide?

options.a: Hydraulic pressure for the normal braking system
options.b: Hydraulic pressure for the alternate braking system

question: Which needle on the triple pressure indicator shows the supply pressure from the alternate braking accumulator?

options.a: The bottom left needle

options.c: The bottom right needle

question: When following the MLG Nitrogen Filling procedure (Metric), what is the HA dimension used for?

options.a: To determine the maximum aircraft weight

question: What is the acceptable tolerance for the measured H dimension when compared to the target HA value in the shock absorber check?

options.a: ± 1 mm
options.c: ± 33 mm

options.a: PA must be greater than PB by 10 bar

question: What is the minimum H dimension threshold below which inflation with the aircraft on jacks is required?

question: Why is it critical to ensure the floating piston is at the top of the bottom chamber during shock absorber servicing?

question: Which component in the Honeywell APU Fuel Control Unit (FCU) senses fuel temperature for the ECB?

question: What is the primary function of the torque motor in the APU Fuel Control Unit?

options.c: To provide mechanical rotation to the flow divider

question: How does the ECB modulate the APU fuel schedule during on-speed operation?

options.a: Based solely on the ADIRU altitude signal
options.b: To match aircraft demand for bleed air and electrical power
options.c: By maintaining a fixed fuel-to-air ratio regardless of load

question: On the Honeywell APU, what provides the power to operate the surge control valve actuator and the IGV actuator?

options.a: High-pressure pneumatic air

options.c: Yellow system hydraulic pressure

question: What happens to the fuel trapped in the lines to the nozzles when a Honeywell APU shutdown is initiated?

question: At what speed does the flow divider solenoid valve close during a cold start or high-altitude start on a Honeywell APU?

options.a: During the first 7% speed
options.b: During the first 30% speed

question: Which solenoid valve is de-energized by the ECB to effect an APU shutdown?

options.a: The de-oiling solenoid valve

options.c: The IGV servo solenoid

question: When checking the APU fuel filter on the Honeywell variant, what component provides a mechanical indication of an impending clog?

options.a: The fuel pump pressure switch

options.c: The 3-way shutoff valve position indicator

question: What prevents excessive fuel pressure peaks in the APU high-pressure fuel line?

options.a: The delta pressure regulator
options.b: A pressure relief valve in the HP pump

question: During Honeywell APU start, when does the 3-way shutoff solenoid valve move to the open position?

options.a: Immediately when the START P/B is pressed

options.c: At 50% RPM

question: On the Honeywell APU, which component directs air into the load compressor?

options.b: The compressor outlet scroll
options.c: The exhaust diffuser
